title: Combat
summary: Attacking, summoning sickness, blocking, damage and combat keywords.

checklist.label: I know why new creatures can't attack
I can work out which creatures are destroyed
I know Flying, Trample, Deathtouch and First strike

steps.title: Attacking
steps.body:
In combat, you choose which of your untapped creatures [[attack]]. You [[tap]] them as they attack.

Attackers go after your opponent, or one of their planeswalkers.

You can attack with all, some or none of your creatures. It's always your choice.

visual.src: Two creatures turning sideways as they attack the opponent.

steps.title: Summoning sickness
steps.body:
A creature can't attack on the turn it arrives. Players call this [[summoning-sickness|summoning sickness]].

The rule: a creature can attack only if you've controlled it **since the start of your turn**.

Creatures with [[haste|Haste]] ignore this rule and can attack right away.

visual.src: A newly cast creature with a small New tag, waiting, next to a Haste creature already attacking.
visual.altText: A new creature waiting, and a Haste creature attacking.

check.question: You cast a creature without Haste this turn. Can it attack this turn?

options.text: No, it has to wait until my next turn

check.hint: Only Haste lets a creature attack the turn it arrives.

steps.title: Blocking
steps.body:
Now your opponent chooses blockers. Each of their untapped creatures may [[block]] one attacker. Blocking doesn't tap a creature, and several creatures can block the same attacker.

- **Blocked** attackers and their blockers deal damage to each other.
- **Unblocked** attackers deal their damage to the player or planeswalker they attacked.

Blocking is optional too.

visual.src: One attacker blocked by a creature, and another attacker going unblocked to hit the player.
visual.altText: One blocked attacker and one unblocked attacker.

steps.title: Combat damage
steps.body:
All combat damage happens **at the same time**.

Each creature deals damage equal to its power. A creature with damage equal to or more than its toughness is destroyed.

Example: a 3/3 blocks a 2/2. The 2/2 takes 3 and is destroyed. The 3/3 takes 2 and survives. That damage wears off at the end of the turn.

visual.src: A 3/3 and a 2/2 trading blows: the 2/2 is destroyed, the 3/3 survives with 2 damage marked.
visual.altText: A 3/3 blocking a 2/2: only the 2/2 is destroyed.

check.question: Your 3/3 attacks. Your opponent blocks with a 2/4. What happens?
check.hint: Compare each creature's power with the other creature's toughness.

steps.title: Combat keywords
steps.body:
Keywords change how combat works:

- [[flying|Flying]]: only Flying or Reach creatures can block it.
- [[trample|Trample]]: extra damage beyond what destroys its blockers goes to the player.
- [[deathtouch|Deathtouch]]: any damage it deals to a creature destroys it.
- [[first-strike|First strike]]: deals its damage before other creatures.

You'll practise these at the Practice Table.

visual.src: Four small scenes: a flyer passing over a ground blocker, a trampler pushing damage through, a deathtouch snake defeating a giant, and a first-striking knight hitting first.

check.question: A 1/1 with Deathtouch blocks a 5/5. What happens?
check.hint: The 5/5 deals plenty of damage. And Deathtouch makes even 1 damage enough.
